brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Stacked full hex bases at (0,0,0) and (0,0,1) with adjacent full bases (1,0,0)+(1,0,1) and half-n caps forming a vertical 2-level tower, verified by get_build and check_build clear
Two drawers installed: drawer:0#0,1#cut at level 0 south side and drawer:1#0,1#cut at level 1 south side, both seating on half-n bases
Open bins added on top level (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full and bin:0,1,1~hex-bin-half-n-full) for workbench small parts; overall structure capped and bolted (capOpenFaces + lockJoints) forming stable tower

finish.summary: Built a 2-storey tower: two vertical columns (0,0 and 1,0) each two levels high, with north half-cells providing drawer fronts. Installed two stacked south-facing drawers (levels 0 and 1) plus two open bins on the upper level for workbench parts storage. All open faces capped and joints locked, mesh clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
